Managing AI agents is a big part of Lotte Underwood's job

Recent university graduate Lotte Underwood is a public relations executive with a twist - she spends more time using AI than actually doing PR.

Underwood, 25, joined London-based PR agency Fight or Flight in November last year, in the new role of "AI associate" after completing a degree and then a masters in marketing.

She's part of a recently established, dedicated AI team that has built around 30 AI agents. Specific tasks include industry research, client reporting, media interview preparation, helping clients create clearer briefs, and image generation.

A big part of Underwood's job is to manage those agents, check their outputs and feed those to the team members who are dealing directly with clients and the media.

Another key responsibility of hers is to monitor how clients appear in the responses from AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and others.

"A huge part is being in client meetings and calls to work out what is actually going to be most helpful from these agents," says Underwood.

AI is seen as one of the main factors behind graduate job cuts , but companies are also creating dedicated AI-specific graduate roles like Underwood's.

Dillan Patel, for example, joined engineering software company Stride 18 months ago as an intern. A business management graduate, he was put to work developing an internal chatbot designed to capture the knowledge of a senior staff member transitioning into retirement.

Patel, 24, is now an AI automation analyst, tasked with developing further internal agents to provide specific information to individual teams, while also identifying which manual or repetitive tasks across the company could be done by AI.

"My role focuses on finding practical ways to use technology, automation, data and AI to improve how we operate," says Coventry-based Patel.

Debra Maxwell is looking for "AI disruptors"

Such AI savvy graduates are also in demand from companies like ArvatoConnect, an outsourced contact centre company.

CEO Debra Maxwell says the company's usual graduate intake is on hold this year, but she plans to resume it next year with a bigger focus on AI.

"We would be looking for more AI-disruptor type roles, where you can challenge us as an organisation to think more holistically about where AI can be applied and where we could grow our business from," says London-based Maxwell.

"We see our graduates as not filling administrative roles, but actually adding value to the organisation in a different way."

Maxwell adds: "For example, one of our recent graduates is using AI to do deep dives on specific markets, and provide more information for when we're bidding [for new contracts]. It's basically giving him a more rounded role."

If AI can make a graduate job bigger and more integral to the organisation, Maxwell argues that companies can create a more loyal, engaged workforce that is able to contribute more meaningfully, much earlier.

Research from consultancy PwC found that some graduate roles are assuming more responsibilities because of AI, as it allows companies to demand more senior abilities from junior hires.

For the consultancy's 2026 AI Jobs Barometer , external , it analysed 2.4 million entry-level jobs in the US. It found that the entry-level roles most influenced by AI are now seven times more likely to require traditionally senior-level skills. These include motivational leadership, strategic decision making and team building.

Those entry-level roles with higher expectations have in fact grown 35% since 2019, PwC found, while other entry-level roles actually shrank by 10%.

Cian Clinton uses around ten AI agents for work tasks

Cian Clinton, who joined consultancy Valliance last September after graduating from a Bachelor of Science in 2024, says the incorporation of AI into his role makes him feel less like a graduate, and more like an equal team member. He uses around 10 AI agents daily for different tasks.

"Your ideas and your creativity are a lot more valued because you actually get to implement those firsthand, and the responsibility you take on is a lot greater because of that," says London-based Clinton, 23.

"I am now taking on responsibilities which would usually take me four or five years to get to."

His career progression, he believes, will now be faster as a result.

"AI is killing the 'pyramid' approach…progression is no longer based on your knowledge bank. Now it's more based on your critical thinking and understanding of the processes," says Clinton.

There's no doubt Underwood, Patel and Clinton are developing valuable AI knowledge which can help them across their careers.

But with their time at work so focused on AI, does it matter how much - or how little - time they're spending learning about the professional field they're supposed to be operating in?

Underwood says she'd like to still pick up the traditional PR skills her role isn't currently focused on, but is confident of her future in the agency's growing AI team.

"There's certain things that I haven't had the chance to do yet, like directly pitching to the media. I absolutely plan to do this," she says.

Graduates becoming too AI-centric is an issue for Simon Pratt, chief operating officer at Portman Finance Group. He says being able to use AI effectively is important, but the company's two-year graduate programme is fully centred on "learning the trade".

"Our graduates rotate across four areas at six-month intervals, working directly alongside senior relationship managers to learn their trade," Northampton-based Pratt explains.

"They'll learn all of our financial products, how to draft credit papers for submission to lenders, and how to build meaningful relationships with our customers. They'll progress to running transactions from start to finish."

Claire Reid, PwC UK's chief technology and innovation officer, believes graduate roles that are too AI heavy won't necessarily provide graduates long-term career progression.

"There will be no graduate job now that doesn't require a baseline of AI literacy," says Glasgow-based Reid.

"But AI skills on their own are not going to help you in your career. You've got to couple that with that sector knowledge of what that client actually wants."

Back in Coventry, Dillan Patel is confident his AI work will continue to be valuable, and he wants to keep building on it.

"I don't think I'd want to explore different positions within the business. Through my involvement in AI-related projects, I already work closely with different areas of the business and I'm gaining valuable knowledge and experience along the way," he says.

New blood tests designed to check for multiple cancers in one go will be offered to NHS patients in some 200 GP surgeries in England as part of a trial.

The aim is to detect hard-to-diagnose abdominal cancers, including liver, ovarian and pancreatic cancer, much sooner. These cancers are often found only after they have spread.

The tests look for proteins or fragments of DNA in the blood that may signal cancer. Results could help doctors decide which patients with vague symptoms need further investigations.

More than 20,000 patients aged 45 and over with symptoms such as pain or persistent bloating will be eligible to take part.

The government-funded trial, led by the University of Birmingham, will assess whether the tests are accurate enough for wider NHS use.

The idea of a blood test that can identify multiple cancers is not new.

A separate NHS trial of a test called Galleri recently failed to meet its main goal of reducing diagnoses of late-stage cancers, although researchers are still assessing its potential benefits.

Prof Peter Johnson, NHS England's national clinical director for cancer, said detecting abdomen cancer early was "notoriously difficult" because symptoms can easily be mistaken for other less serious conditions.

Earlier diagnosis gives patients a much better chance of successful treatment and survival.

Around 71,000 people in England are diagnosed each year with pancreatic, stomach, liver, ovarian or bowel cancer, and nearly 35,000 die from these diseases.

The new STRIDE-RCT trial , external is about detecting bowel, small bowel, stomach, oesophageal, pancreatic, liver, bile duct and gallbladder, ovarian, endometrial, kidney, bladder and prostate cancer.

Patients will provide one or two tubes of blood, taken at their GP practice, alongside routine tests.

Scientists will then analyse the samples for signs of cancer and, if present, may be able to pinpoint where in the body the tumour is located.

A positive result does not automatically mean there is cancer, and a negative result is not a guaranteed all-clear.

Health secretary Yvette Cooper said she hoped simple blood tests such as these would help identify patients needing urgent investigation much sooner.

Michelle Mitchell from Cancer Research UK said: "GPs have long needed better tools to help them navigate that uncertainty by identifying which patients require further testing and this trial in England is an important step towards addressing that need."

More than 500 parties are contesting the elections

South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC).

This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes.

Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations.

Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection.

For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern. The party had a disastrous showing in the last national election, when it lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since 1994 when the racist apartheid system ended.

Support for the party has been dropping significantly over the years because of anger over high levels of corruption, unemployment and crime.

At its peak, in 2004, the ANC got 70% of the vote in the general election. Two decades later its share dropped to 40%.

Polls and pundits have predicted a further loss in these elections but President Cyril Ramaphosa has denied that his party was in a downward spiral.

"What I'm seeing here is that the ANC is going higher and higher and on the 4th [of November] we will show those naysayers," he told supporters at the party's final election rally on Sunday.

In townships like Alexandra, north-east of Johannesburg, the ANC has traditionally had a strong supporter base but poor governance and voter apathy are unravelling this support.

The BBC visited the sprawling township a week before the elections and spoke to residents to get their views. One of them was Sanele Ntombela, who is a first-time voter excited to make his voice heard.

Sanele Ntombela (left), seen here with his friends Tshiamo Mbange (centre) and Lwandle Dladla, is excited to cast his vote

We found the 18-year-old hanging out with his friends on a street corner. Most of his friends said they had no intention of voting and had not registered to do so.

They cited a lack of change and deteriorating delivery of basic services.

But Ntombela was looking forward to voting for the first time and thought it might lead to change.

"We face many challenges in Alexandra. There's rubbish everywhere and we struggle with electricity and water and many other issues," he said.

Just metres away, heaps of rubbish lay gathered beneath a streetlight pole covered in election posters from the different political parties.

On the other side of the street, drain water trickles through the many potholes that have gutted that part of the road.

The ANC faces immense pressure to reverse years of decline

The BBC also spoke to Zandile Mncube, who said she wouldn't vote, even though she is registered to do so.

The 33-year-old woman also cited poor service delivery and performance by local leaders for her decision.

"It makes no difference [whether I vote or not]. Things have gotten worse over the years," she said.

Alex, as the township is known, is a stone's throw away from Sandton, Africa's richest square mile, but the differences could not be starker.

Sandton is known for its skyscrapers, designer shops and well-maintained roads but in Alex, houses are sandwiched together and rubbish, either piled together or left strewn across the pavement, is everywhere. The stench of raw sewage and uncollected rubbish is heavy in the air, but residents appear used to it.

The issues plaguing Alexandra are not unique. A drive around Gauteng province reveals similar patterns of neglect and disrepair, especially in the townships.

South of Johannesburg, Soweto looks marginally cleaner than Alexandra, but residents also complain about service delivery.

Mduduzi Makhubo, 45, has lived in Soweto his entire life and he told the BBC of the community's daily struggles with accessing water and electricity.

"Every Monday we know we won't have water after 2pm," he said.

Makhubo is registered to vote and intends to use his vote to deal with the "arrogance" he says local leaders have towards residents and "change the status quo".

Can this man broaden the appeal of a South African party seen by some as 'too white'?

South Africa's political marriage of convenience avoids divorce - just

These areas offer a small, but important, glimpse into the state of South Africa's local governance.

Years of reports by the auditor-general have highlighted the dire state of most of South Africa's 257 municipalities.

A recent report only gave 39 clean audits - the highest ranking a public entity can achieve - between 2024 and 2025. None of Gauteng's three metro cities, Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, featured in this list.

Earlier this year auditor-general Tsakani Maluleke said Johannesburg "needs ongoing attention".

"If we don't that, we are going to continue on this slide where financial health deteriorates [and] where service delivery continues to be compromised, which is what we are living," she told lawmakers.

The city has been labelled "effectively bankrupt" due to the dire state of its finances. Dirty streets, unstable electricity supply and persistent water issues have been common for years.

Experts the BBC spoke to agreed that all eyes will be on Africa's wealthiest city as well as the country's seven other biggest municipalities, or metros, particularly those in Gauteng when the results come in.

Of South Africa's eight metros, only three are governed by a single party. In Gauteng, all three metros are governed by coalition governments, with the ANC the largest party.

Political analyst Melanie Verwoerd said the elections would be a "verdict ... and judgment" on the ANC.

"And the expectation is that the ANC generally in the country is going to [perform] the worst it's ever done," she said.

Several polls point to a continued decline in support for the party in Wednesday's election, contested by over 500 political parties.

One, conducted by Ipsos, put the ANC's support at 30%, down from the 46% it got at the last local elections in 2021.

The same poll, along with others, points to a slight increase in electoral support for the Democratic Alliance (DA), especially in Johannesburg. Ipsos predicts the DA will garner 25% support in this election, up from 22% last time.

DA leader Helen Zille has been vying for the mayoral chain in the city and her unusual campaign has attracted a lot of attention.

The former Cape Town mayor has been captured swimming in crater-sized potholes, ziplining over sinkholes and riding into her final rally in the city in a classic BMW 325i, known locally as a "Gusheshe".

She believes the DA is the country's best choice for a government, telling local radio broadcaster 702 last week that "towns and cities that work best are under DA governance".

Verwoerd, a former ANC MP and South Africa's ambassador to Ireland, predicted that coalitions would continue being the order of the day across Gauteng.

These types of arrangements have often been viewed as unstable and chaotic at a local level and the constant change in leadership, usually caused by parties falling out with each other, has affected service delivery in many municipalities.

Zandile Mncube says things have got worse in her township over the years

Verwoerd said in her view, the most stable coalitions would be those that replicate what the ANC and DA have done on a national level, where the historic rivals have agreed to share power.

Reflecting on Cape Town, she said it was unlikely that the DA would lose control of the municipality. The coastal city is widely considered the country's best-performing metro and has been run by the DA since the late 2000s when it unseated the ANC.

Ethekwini, which includes the port city of Durban in KwaZulu-Natal, would be a "different story", Verwoerd said.

The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party has been projected to perform well in the area but it is unclear if it will secure the outright majority needed to run the metro. Polls suggest it won't and will need partners to form a government.

The party was founded by former South African President Jacob Zuma and was the biggest party across his home province of KwaZulu-Natal in the 2024 provincial election.

Verwoerd reflected that while various options were on the table for the party, forming a government would be "very messy" given its refusal to work with either the ANC or DA.

A confident Zuma, addressing supporters on Sunday, vowed to take control of a number of municipalities after the elections.

Another political analyst Dr Levy Ndou echoed Verwoerd's assessment, saying that a coalition between the DA and ANC seemed unavoidable in most metros.

"We're not sure whether the arrangement of the government of national unity could have the potential to influence how the metros are going to be run," he said.

Both experts also spoke about the declining voter turnout in South Africa's elections. Over 29 million citizens are registered to vote, but the turnout, especially among young people, has seen a steady decline.

Ndou attributed this to the "calibre" of the candidates campaigning and the lack of visibility of local councillors, who are often the ones elected to lead their neighbourhoods, in election campaigns.

South Africa's electoral commission has seven days to announce the results, but parties have 14 days to form a governing structure.

Ishyirahamwe ry’Umukino wa Basketball muri Amerika (NBA) ryatangaje ko rizakomeza ubufatanye n’u Rwanda, nubwo Abasenateri babiri bo muri Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika barisabye kongera gusuzuma imikoranire yaryo narwo, bitwaje impungenge zijyanye n’uburenganzira bwa muntu n’umutekano mu Karere. Mu ibaruwa yashyizwe ahagaragara, Komiseri Wungirije wa NBA, Mark Tatum, yasubije Abasenateri Jeff Merkley wo mu Ishyaka ry’Aba-Demokarate na Marsha Blackburn wo mu Ishyaka ry’Aba-Repubulikani, bari bandikiye Komiseri wa NBA, Adam Silver, basaba ibisobanuro ku bufatanye bw’iri shyirahamwe n’u Rwanda.

Aba basenateri bavuze ko bahangayikishijwe n’uko NBA ikomeje kwagura imikoranire n’u Rwanda, mu gihe bashinja Guverinoma y’u Rwanda kugira uruhare mu bibazo by’umutekano mu Burasirazuba bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, ndetse no kutubahiriza uburenganzira bwa muntu.

Ntabwo aribyo gusa kuko banavuze ko ubufatanye bushingiye kuri Siporo bushobora gukoreshwa mu kunoza isura y’Igihugu mu gihe hari ibibazo nk’ibyo bashingiraho bitwaza, ibyo bita sportswashing.

Mu gusubiza, Tatum yavuze ko NBA igendera kuri politiki ya Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika mu gufata ibyemezo bijyanye n’ibihugu ikoreramo ibikorwa by’ubucuruzi.

Yagize ati: “Ibikorwa byacu mu bihugu bitandukanye ntibishingira ku buryo bumwe, ariko muri byose dukurikiza politiki ya Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika mu kugena aho dukorera n’uburyo dukoramo.”

Yongeyeho ko NBA yamagana ihohoterwa ry'uburenganzira bwa muntu aho ryaba ribera hose, kandi ko izakomeza guhindura imikorere yayo uko impinduka muri politiki ya Amerika zizabisaba.

Mu kugaragaza uko NBA ishyira mu bikorwa iyo politiki, Tatum yagarutse ku ikipe ya APR Basketball Club, yagombaga kwitabira irushanwa rya Basketball Africa League (BAL). Iyi kipe isanzwe ari iya Minisiteri y’Ingabo z'u Rwanda ntabwo yakinnye irushanwa rya BAL rya 2026 nyuma y’ibihano Amerika yafatiye Ingabo z’u Rwanda muri Werurwe 2026.

Tatum yavuze ko ariyo mpamvu APR itazemererwa kongera gukina muri BAL igihe ibyo bihano bizaba bitarakurwaho.

Ubusanzwe ufatanye bw’u Rwanda na NBA burimo kwakira imikino ya Basketball Africa League muri BK Arena yakira abagera ku bihumbi 10.

Nyuma y'aho abademokarate begukanye intsinzi ikomeye yabahaye umwiganze mu nteko no muri Sena, bamwe mu bagize Ishyaka ry'Abarepubulikani batangiye gushinja Perezida Donald Trump uruhare rukomeye muri ayo makuba yageze ku ishyaka ryabo.

Umwe mu baharanira inyungu z'Abarepubulikani, Bill Miller, yavuze ko nta wundi wabazwa ayo makuba uretse Trump ubwe.

Yagize ati: "Ni we ubwe ubiryozwa. Nta wundi. Ibi ni ukwanga no gutera umugongo Perezida Trump mu buryo bwuzuye."

Yakomeje avuga ko ibyabaye ari "amakuba akomeye cyane" kandi ko nta muntu wari witeze ko ibintu byarangira muri ubwo buryo.

Mu Ishyaka ry'Abarepubulikani, ihungabana ryatewe n'ibyavuye mu matora ryahise risimburwa n'uburakari bukomeye bwibasiye Perezida Trump.

Nyuma y'uko Abademokarate batsinze mu buryo butunguranye no mu bice byari bisanzwe bifatwa nk'ibihome by'Abarepubulikani nka Texas, Kansas na South Carolina, bamwe mu badepite n'abajyanama b'ishyaka bavuze ko Trump yibanze cyane ku murage we wa politiki aho kwita ku bibazo byahangayikishaga abaturage.

Gregg Peppin, umuhanga mu ngamba za politiki mu Ishyaka ry'Abarepubulikani, yavuze ko habayeho amakosa menshi akurikirana.

Yagize ati: "Byari amakosa akurikirana nta gahenge. Biragaragara ko muri leta nyinshi abaturage batishimiye politiki za Perezida."

Umwe mu bafatanyabikorwa ba Trump muri White House na we yavuze ko umujinya abaturage bafitiye Perezida wari umaze kugera ku rwego rwo hejuru, cyane cyane nyuma y'intambara ya Iran, imisoro ku bicuruzwa bitumizwa mu mahanga n'ingamba zikomeye zafashwe ku bimukira, ibintu yavuze ko byahuriranye bikagira ingaruka zikomeye ku matora.

Ku ruhande rwa Visi Perezida wa Amerika, JD Vance yavuze ko impamvu nyamukuru yatumye Abarepubulikani batsindwa ari intambara ya Iran.

Mu butumwa burebure yashyize ku rubuga X, Vance yagize ati: "Impamvu twatsinzwe ni intambara."

Vance yemeye ko intambara ya Iran, izamuka ry'ikiguzi cy'ubuzima ndetse n'ibindi bibazo byatumye bamwe mu batoye we na Perezida Donald Trump mu matora yo muri 2024 batera umugongo Ishyaka ry'Abarepubulikani muri uyu mwaka.

Yavuze kandi ko hari abaturage batishimiye politiki ya guverinoma ku bibazo by'abimukira, yongeraho ko yiteguye gushyigikira amavugurura kuri zimwe muri izo gahunda.

Vance yanagaragaje ko na Trump ubwe yavuze ko abaturage bagaragaje kutishimira intambara ya Iran mu matora. Gusa, nyuma y'amezi menshi ashyigikira iyo ntambara ku mugaragaro, Vance yavuze yeruye kurushaho ko ari imwe mu mpamvu nyamukuru yatumye ishyaka rye ritsindwa.

Iri tangazo ryahise rituma benshi batangira kuvuga ku migambi ya Vance mu matora y'umukuru w'igihugu ateganyijwe mu 2028. Abasesenguzi ba politiki bamwe bavuga ko ashobora kuba yarakoresheje uyu mwanya kugira ngo atange ibimenyetso by'uko ateganya kwiyamamariza kuyobora Amerika.

Kugeza ubu, Vance yakomeje kwirinda gusubiza ibibazo bijyanye no kuba yakiyamamariza Perezida. Ariko nyuma y'aya matora, arushaho gushyirwaho igitutu cyo gutangaza vuba icyemezo cye ku hazaza h'umwuga we wa politiki.

Ishirahamwe ry'umupira w'amaboko rya Amerika, NBA (National Basketball Association), ritangaza ko ryakuye mw'ihiganwa ryayo rya Afrika umurwi wa basketball w'ingabo z'Urwanda, APR Basketball Club (APR BBC) kubera ibihano Reta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika zafatiye Urwanda muri Ntwarante (3) uyu mwaka.

Imbere y'aha, NBA yari yavuze ko umurwi APR BBC uhabwa uburyo n'igisirikare c'Urwanda utazoja mw'ihiganwa rya Basketball Africa League (BAL) ryo mu 2026.

Ariko rero, ubu ni bwo bwa mbere NBA ishize ahabona icatumye APR ikurwa mw'ihiganwa.

Mu kwa gatatu uno mwaka, ishirahamwe ry'umupira w'amaboko wa Basketball mu Rwanda (FERWABA) ryari ryatangaje ko APR ari yo yari yafashe icemezo co "kwikura mw'iri higanwa".

Ishirahamwe NBA ryatangaje ibi igihe ryariko ryishura ku birego vyatanzwe n'abakenguzamateka babiri ba Amerika, bandikiye NBA bayisaba gusubira kwihweza amasezerano ifitaniye n'uno murwi w'Urwanda.

Muri Ntwarante (3), Amerika yafatiye ibihano igisirikare c'Urwanda, icagiriza uruhara mu gukomeza intambara ibera muri Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (DR Congo).

Abo bakenguzamateka bavuze ko NBA iri mu kaga ko "kwisanga iriko irafasha mu mugambi wo kweza isura y'Urwanda biciye mu nkino, mu kwemera amafaranga atangwa na reta y'Urwanda ibandanya ihonyanga uburenganzira bwa muntu".

Mu ndwi iheze, Amerika yafatiye kandi ibihano ubushikiranganji bw'Urwanda bujejwe kwivuna abansi kubera ugushigikira umuhari w'inyeshamba za M23, wigaruriye ibice binini vyo mu buseruko bwa DR Congo. Urwanda rwamye ruhakana ibi birego nubwo hari ivyemezo vyinshi bivyerekana.

Urwanda ni kimwe mu bihugu vy'abafatanyabikorwa ba BAL kandi ruratanga uburyo kugira ngo inkino za nyuma z'iri higanwa zibere mu nyubakwa ya BK Arena, yakira abantu 10.000, ku mugwa mukuru Kigali.

Mw'ikete ryo ku wa 23 Gitugutu (10) ryandikiwe NBA, umukenguzamateka w'Umudemokarate Jeffrey Merkley hamwe na mugenziwe w'Umurepubulikani Marsha Blackburn basavye ko NBA yobashikiriza inyishu yanditse bitarenze ku wa 2 Munyonyo (2) ku bijanye n'igituma ibandanya ikorana n'Urwanda.

Babajije bati: "Ni uwuhe murongo ntarengwa kuri NBA mu kwemera amafaranga ava mu bihugu bihonyanga uburenganzira bwa muntu?"

Mu bindi bibazo babajije, basavye kumenya ukuntu NBA ishobora guhuza "ingendo yayo yo kubandanya ikorana n'Urwanda n'ivyo ivuga ko ishigikiye ubutungane".

Nk'uko urubuga ngurukanabumenyi rw'inkino rwo muri Amerika ESPN rubivuga, icegera c'umukuru wa NBA, Mark Tatum, mu nyishu yiwe yavuze ko umurwi wa APR "wamaze gukurwa" muri BAL inyuma y'ivyo bihano vyafashwe mu ntango z'umwaka.

NBA yavuze kandi ko APR izobandanya gutaramurwa mu gihe cose ibi bihano vya Amerika bizoba bikiri mu ngiro.

APR ni umwe mu mirwi ikomeye ya basketball mu Rwanda kandi yaraserukiye igihugu muri BAL mu 2024 na 2025, aho yarangije iri mu kibanza ca gatatu. Uyu mwaka yasubirijwe n'umurwi RSSB Tigers.

BAL ni ihiganwa rya basketball rihuza imirwi yo muri Afrika ryatangujwe kandi ritegurirwa hamwe na NBA be n'ishirahamwe mpuzamakungu rya basketball FIBA.

Ni ihiganwa rihuza imirwi 12 iva mu bihugu bitandukanye vya Afrika.

Kuva BAL itanguye mu 2021, Urwanda rwakiriye inkino zose za nyuma n'izo gukuranamwo havuyemwo rimwe gusa.

NBA ivugwa ko ironka buri mwaka amamiriyoni y'amadorari atanzwe n'Urwanda biciye mu masezerano y'ugukorana n'uburenganzira bwo kwamamaza.

DR Congo imaze igihe yiyamiriza amasezerano mpuzamakungu akomeye y'Urwanda mu vy'inkino, harimwo ayo rufitaniye na NBA, imirwi y'umupira w'amaguru yo ku mugabane wa Buraya hamwe na Formula 1, isaba ko afutwa.

Congo ivuga ko ayo masezerano afasha Urwanda kweza isura yarwo ku rwego mpuzamakungu, mu gihe intambara zibandanya mu buseruko bwa DR Congo.

Amatora yo hagati muri manda yabaye ejo ku wa kabiri yabaye akaga kadasanzwe ku ishaya ry'aba-Repubilikani batakaje ubwiganze muri Sena no mu Nteko Ishinga mategeko.

Hejuru y'ibyo, ni amatora abayemwo ibintu bitangaje, bibaye ubwa mbere mu mateka y'amatora, aho hatowe abantu batari bamenyerewe muri politique y'Amerika.

Uwa mbere ni Abdul El-Sayed azaba Umusenateri wa mbere w'Umuyisilamu muri Amerika, nyuma y'uko ibyavuye mu matora by'agateganyo bigaragaje ko yatsinze umukandida w'Ishyaka ry'Aba-Repubulikani, Mike Rogers, muri Leta ya Michigan.

El-Sayed yagiye ahura n'ibitero by'amagambo by'abanyapolitiki b'Aba-Repubulikani, kugeza no kuri Perezida Donald Trump, bamushinjaga cyangwa bakavuga mu buryo buziguye ko uyu muganga w'inzobere mu ndwara z'ibyorezo wavukiye muri Michigan atari Umunyamerika kandi ko ashyigikira iterabwoba.

Trump yamwise "umuntu ufite ibitekerezo bikabije kandi bishobora guteza akaga," "umuntu ukabya mu bitekerezo," ndetse amwita "Mohammed." El-Sayed n'abamushyigikiye barabinenze bavuga ko bigamije guheza Abayisilamu no gushingira ku ivangura rishingiye ku idini cyangwa ku bwoko, bikaba binabangamira ubwisanzure bw'imyemerere.

Hari kandi na Kiesha Lance Bottoms azaba umugore wa mbere w'Umunyamerika ufite inkomoko muri Afurika utorewe kuyobora Leta muri Amerika, nyuma yo gutsinda amatora yo kuyobora Leta ya Georgia, ahanganye na Rick Jackson wo mu Ishyaka ry'Aba-Republicains.

Bottoms wahoze ari umuyobozi w'umujyi wa Atlanta, yari ahanganye na Rick Jackson, umuherwe ukora ibikorwa by'ubucuruzi.

Chris Pappas wo muri Leta ya New Hampshire na we azaba umugabo wa mbere wagaragaje ku mugaragaro ko ari umutinganyi (gay) uzaba umu senateri muri Amerika.

Yatsinze John E. Sununu, wahoze ari Senateri w'Ishyaka ry'Aba-Repubulikani muri Amerika, akaba yarigeze gukorera mu mitwe yombi igize Inteko Ishinga Amategeko ya Amerika.

Hariho kandi na Deb Haaland, umugore wa mbere w'umunyamerika w'umusangwabutaka (Native Americans) watorewe kuba Guverineri wa Leta muri Amerika. Yatangajwe ko yatsinze umukandida w'Aba-Republicains, Gregg Hull, bityo akaba agiye kuyobora Leta ya New Mexico.

Mu mwaka wa 2018, Haaland yari umwe mu bagore babiri ba mbere b'abasangwabutaka batorewe kujya mu Nteko Ishinga Amategeko ya Amerika (Congress).

Nyuma yaje kuba umuntu wa mbere ukomoka muri abo basangwabutaka wagizwe Umunyamabanga wa Guverinoma (Cabinet Secretary), ubwo yari ashinzwe Minisiteri y'Umutungo Kamere n'Ubutaka mu butegetsi bwa Perezida Joe Biden.

Amerika ishobora kuva ku kuba yari ifite ba guverineri batatu b'Abirabura gusa batowe mu mateka yayo y'imyaka 250, ikagira abandi barindwi bashya mu ijoro rimwe.

Ku wa kabiri, Guverineri wa Maryland, Wes Moore, wabaye Guverineri wa gatatu w'Umwirabura muri Amerika kandi akaba ari na we wenyine wari ukiri ku butegetsi, yongeye gutsinda amatora yo kuyobora iyo Leta.

Hagati aho, Byron Donalds wo mu Ishyaka ry'Aba-Republicains yatorewe kuba Guverineri wa mbere w'Umwirabura wa Leta ya Florida.

Nyuma y'intsinzi ya Bottoms muri Georgia, Leta ebyiri zo mu majyepfo y'Amerika zizaba ziyobowe n'Abirabura ku nshuro ya mbere mu mateka yazo.

Uretse Leta ya Minnesota, izo mpinduka zishobora no gutuma haboneka abandi ba Guverineri b'Abirabura muri Wisconsin, Nevada, South Carolina na Michigan.

Umunyamerika yavukiye muri Ethiopia yemeye imbere y'ubutungane ko yahaye Ethiopia amakuru y'iperereza y'ibanga akomeye kandi yari akingiwe cane, harimwo n'ayo yari yizeye ko yashobora gufasha mu gutera, gutumbereza no kwica abarwanyi mu gihe c'intambara y'imbere mu gihugu yabaye mu 2020.

Abraham Teklu Lemma, yahoze afitaniye amasezerano y'akazi na reta ya Amerika, yemeye ko yamaze imyaka irenga ibiri aguma aha abategetsi bakuru ba Ethiopia inyandiko n'amafoto vyinshi vyarimwo amakuru y'ibanga, nk'uko ubushikiranganji bw'ubutungane bwa Reta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika bubivuga.

Jeanine Ferris Pirro, umushikirizamanza wa Amerika mu karere ka Columbia, yagize ati: "Mu gukora ivyo, yahemukiye indahiro, abo bakorana hamwe n'igihugu ciwe, yongera ashira mu kaga umutekano w'igihugu cacu."

Lemma, afise imyaka 54, ashobora gukatirwa igihano co gupfungwa gushika ku myaka 22, hisunzwe amasezerano yagiranye n'ubushikirizamanza yo kwemera icaha. Bitegekanijwe ko urubanza ruzosomwa muri Ndamukiza (4) umwaka uza.

Abraham yari yarakoze, ku masezerano afise igihe amara, mu bushikiranganji bwa Amerika bujejwe imigenderanire, ubushikiranganji bw'ubutungane, hamwe no mu rwego rujejwe ibigendajuru bikoreshwa mw'iperereza rya Amerika.

Abashikirizamanza bavuze ko yakoranye n'abategetsi bakuru bo mu nzego za politike, igisirikare n'iperereza muri Ethiopia hagati ya 2021 n'igihe yafatwa muri Myandagaro(8) 2023.

Yakuye, mu mpisho, inyandiko n'ibindi bikoresho birimwo amakuru y'ibanga mu nyubakwa za reta zikingiwe cane, rimwe rimwe amakuru y'agaciro kanini akayakoporora ku mpapuro akoresheje ikaramu, akabijana hanze y'izo nyubakwa. Yarakoresheje ububasha bw'ubuhinga yari afise mu kazi ko gucungera ivyuma n'imihora y'imashini nyabwonko (IT) kugira ngo atware amadosiye ku makuru y'iperereza yari abitswe mu buryo bwa none.

Abashikirizamanza bavuze bati: "Amakuru menshi y'ibanga rikomeye Lemma yahaye reta ya Ethiopia yari yerekeye intambara muri Ethiopia."

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Ayo makuru yarimwo amasanamu yafashwe n'ibigendajuru hamwe n'ayerekeye ibikorwa vy'igisirikare, akaba yayashikirije abategetsi ba Ethiopia akoresheje ubutumwa bwahinyanyuwe ku buryo bigoye ko abandi babusoma.

Urwego rw'iperereza rwa Amerika, FBI, rwavuze ko abategetsi ba Ethiopia bahavuye bakoresha mu bikorwa vya gisirikare amakuru y'iperereza bahawe na Abraham.

Abashikirizamanza bavuze ko yari yiteze ko ayo makuru yofasha igisirikare ca Ethiopia kumenya aho abarwanyi baherereye gurtyo kibone kubica.

John Eisenberg, icegera c'umushikirizamanza mukuru wa Amerika ku mutekano w'igihugu, yavuze ati: "Lemma yahemukiye Reta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika ku rugero rudasanzwe."

Mu butumwa yandikiye umutegetsi umwe wa Ethiopia muri Kigarama (12) 2021, [Abraham] yanditse ati: "Dutegerezwa guheraheza abo bantu rimwe na rizima, ahandi ho nta mahoro azokwigera aboneka muri Ethiopia", nk'uko bigaragazwa n'inyandiko zo muri sentare.

Mu nyuma kuri uwo musi nyene, yarungikiye uwo mutegetsi ayandi makuru y'iperereza, amusaba ati: "Ndabingize, rungike ama drones."

Ukumenyekana kw'ibi gutanga umuco ku kungene amakuru y'iperereza ya Amerika y'agaciro kanini cane yahawe abategetsi ba Ethiopia mu gihe c'intambara y'imbere mu gihugu yatikije inganda, ikaba yishe abantu ibihumbi amajana, yongera ituma abandi amamiliyoni bata izabo.

Abraham yafatiwe muri reta ya Maryland muri Myandagaro (8) 2023, inyuma y'itohoza ryari ryerekeye ingene yafata canke yatunganya amakuru y'ibanga ajanye n'iperereza.

Ico gihe, abashikirizamanza bamwagirije ko yari yarakuyeko ibimenyetso vyerekana ko raporo z'iperereza ari iz'ibanga, maze agashikiriza ayo makuru umukozi w'urwego rw'iperereza rw'ikindi gihugu.

Mu butumwa bumwe, uwo mukozi w'iperereza yaramusavye kubandanya amufasha, maze Lemma amwishura ati: "Roger that!" (ubutumwa bwashitse!), bisobanura ko yari yemeye kubikora.

Pirro, wa mushikirizamanza wa Amerika, yavuze ko Abraham yakoresheje nabi uburenganzira yari afise bwo gushikira amwe mu makuru y'iperereza ya Amerika kandi y'ibanga rikomeye cane.

Yamwagirije guhemukira abo bakorana hamwe n'igihugu ciwe. Abashikirizamanza bavuze ko "azokurikiranwa mu butungane gushika ku rugero rwose rutegekanywa n'amategeko".

Abraham yemeye imbere y'ubutungane ko yagize uruhara mu mugambi wo gushikiriza reta y'ikindi gihugu amakuru yerekeye ivyo kwivuna abansi ya Amerika.

Bitegekanijwe ko azocirwa urubanza kw'igenekerezo rya 14 Ndamukiza (4) 2027.

Iyo ntambara yamaze imyaka ibiri, ikaba yari yatanguye muri Munyonyo (11) 2020, yashamiranya ku ruhande rumwe ingabo za reta nkuru ya Ethiopia n'abo bacuditse, n'abarwanyi bo mu karere ka Tigray gaherereye mu buraruko bw'ico gihugu, ku rundi ruhande.

Iyo ntambara yaranzwe n'ibirego vyinshi vy'amabi akomeye, harimwo ubwicanyi, ihohotera rishingiye ku gitsina hamwe n'ibitero ku basivire.

Amasezerano y'amahoro yashizweko umukono muri Munyonyo (11) 2022 yarangije intambara nyamukuru, n'ubwo amatati n'umutekano muke vyabandanije muri ako karere.

Watch: Abdul El-Sayed thanks supporters for backing 'unlikeliest of candidates'

It was an unlikely greeting to hear at a Democratic Party victory rally after the US midterm elections.

Abdul El-Sayed , 42, born to Egyptian immigrant parents, playfully addressed Vice-President JD Vance, who had campaigned against him but will now swear him into office in January as Michigan's new Senator.

The US-born Democrat spent much of his campaign fending off attacks from conservative media and President Donald Trump, who accused him of supporting the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed rejected the allegations.

"My name is Abdul Rahman Mohammed El-Sayed," he said in an Egyptian Arabic accent to the cheering crowd at his victory rally. His Arabic Muslim name was a target for many of his opponents. He is set to become the first Muslim senator.

El-Sayed ran a social media-first campaign, with TikTok edits showing him speaking directly to young voters, tapping into Gen Z humour, and sporting friendship bracelets.

The former public health administrator's campaign centred on a progressive agenda, including Medicare for All, affordable housing and curbing corporate influence in politics. He has also been a vocal critic of US military aid to Israel.

But El-Sayed was not alone. From an Ethiopian-born Gen Z congresswoman to candidates with Nigerian heritage, several other politicians with African roots won in this year's midterms.

The elections, held halfway through a president's four-year term, decide who represents Americans in Congress, as well as in thousands of state and local offices.

Born in Addis Ababa, Melat Kiros' family moved to Denver when she was a baby

At 29, Melat Kiros became the first Gen Z woman elected to the US Congress.

Born in Ethiopia, she arrived in the US as a baby and grew up in Denver. She had never held elected office before defeating a 15-term incumbent in Colorado's 1st District in the Democrat primary before winning a landslide in Tuesday's election.

Kiros, like El-Sayed, campaigned on issues that have become central to young progressive voters: the cost of living, universal childcare and Medicare for All.

Endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America, she has also called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement and ending US military aid to Israel.

Her outspoken criticism of Israel's war in Gaza has attracted controversy. Kiros has said her criticism is directed at the Israeli state, not Jewish people.

She was fired from a top New York law firm in 2023 after she refused to take down an open letter to dozens of law firms who had urged law school deans to crack down on antisemitism on campuses as students engaged in pro-Palestinian protests.

Kiros condemned antisemitism, but warned the law firms, including the one she worked for, against conflating "such bigotry with the geo-political question of Israel's legitimacy".

She said she started thinking more seriously about politics in general after being fired.

Adrian Boafo's parents moved from Ghana to the US

Adrian Boafo, meanwhile, a second-generation Ghanaian-American, will represent Maryland's 5th Congressional District after succeeding veteran Congressman Steny Hoyer, who retired after a political career spanning more than four decades.

The 32-year-old was born in Virginia and raised in Prince George's County, Maryland. His parents immigrated to the US from Ghana.

Boafo's route to Congress began in local politics. He served on the Bowie City Council before becoming a Maryland state delegate in 2023. He also worked for Hoyer before eventually winning the race to replace him.

His campaign focused on the cost of living, childcare and protecting federal workers, a major issue in a district close to Washington DC and home to thousands of government employees.

In his victory statement, Boafo said representing his constituents had "never felt more urgent", pointing to federal job cuts, rising costs and the Trump administration's immigration crackdown.

Among those returning to Congress is Somali-born Ilhan Omar, 44, who won a fifth term despite an ongoing federal investigation.

Federal agents searched her Washington home in October as part of an investigation into her immigration paperwork. Omar has denied wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime.

First elected to Congress in 2018, Omar became the first Somali-American and one of the first Muslim women to serve in the chamber. She has also been a frequent target of President Trump, who has repeatedly criticised her and other Somali immigrants.

Trump has previously used derogatory language to describe some African countries, including Somalia. In October, his Yemeni-born adviser Amer Ghalib said the president would refrain from using such language.

Others made their breakthroughs in state and local politics.

Junior Ezeonu was born in Nigeria and moved to the US as a young child. By 27, he had already become Grand Prairie's youngest city council member before winning a seat in the Texas State House.

Then there is Carol Kazeem , 34, a Pennsylvania state legislator of Nigerian heritage who has retained her seat at District 159. At least four candidates with Nigerian heritage won in the 3 November midterms.

For some young Africans watching from across the Atlantic, these victories have offered a glimpse of what a new generation of voters could achieve at home.

On social media, users have shared the election results as a source of inspiration, particularly in Nigeria and Kenya, where major elections are due in 2027.

Bellarmine Mugabe is the youngest son of Zimbabwe's former leader

Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe, the son of Zimbabwe's late former president Robert Mugabe, has been arrested in connection with an assault case, police say.

He was one of five men arrested on Tuesday during a probe into the alleged smuggling , external of two luxury vehicles into Zimbabwe, online news site The New Zimbabwe reports.

According to local media reports, the vehicles have been seized by the Zimbabwe Anti-Corruption Commission.

Mugabe, 29, is the youngest son of Robert Mugabe and his second wife, Grace Mugabe. Robert Mugabe, who died in 2019, ruled Zimbabwe for 37 years before being forced from power at the age of 93 in 2017.

Police said Mugabe was arrested alongside Munashe Mubawu, 43, Terrence Johannes Chinyemba, 42, Fredson Peter, 33, and Solomon Pamire, 34.

All five were arrested in connection with a case of assault which happened at the Brompton Guest Lodge in Harare at about 18:30 local time (16:30 GMT) on 3 November, according to a police statement.

They are due to appear in court on 5 November.

Javits Frimpong was chased down and fatally shot last week on his way to school

The mother of a 15-year-old Ghanaian boy who was fatally shot in the United States last week has left Ghana for America after being granted an emergency visa by President Donald Trump.

"I want justice for my son," Doris Adu Gyamfi told the BBC at the airport before her departure.

She said he had dreamt of becoming a medical doctor.

Her son, Javits Frimpong, who had only been in the US for a year, was chased down and shot on Thursday morning on his way to school in the Bronx, New York.

He was taken to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

Police have not made any arrests and an investigation is ongoing as authorities search for three teenage boys in connection with the shooting.

His death has sparked outrage in both Ghana and the US, and reignited the debate about gun violence in America.

Doris Adu Gyamfi said she was going to the US to help plan her son's funeral

His mother was escorted to the airport by relatives and Dr Erieka Bennett, Head of Mission of the African Diaspora Forum.

"I'm going to America to plan my son's funeral," Gyamfi said.

She thanked the government and well-wishers for their support and prayers following her son's death.

In a social media post on Saturday, New York mayor Zohran Mamdani said Trump had agreed to grant a visa to Gyamfi so she could mourn her son in person.

Mamdani said the murder of a child was a pain no parent should endure, "let alone from thousands of miles away.”

"Javits Frimpong's mother deserves to say goodbye to her son in person. I just got off the phone with President Trump, and he has agreed to grant her visa immediately," he said.

"All of New York City is mourning this tragedy," he added.

Ghana's government has condemned the killing and said it was following the case closely to ensure justice.

It has urged US authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and said it was ready to provide legal and consular support to ensure the perpetrators are brought to justice.

Police are searching for three teenage suspects who fled the scene, captured on surveillance footage.

The shooting has sparked concern among Ghanaians about the safety of children sent to study in America.

Rwanda's army team APR came third in the Basketball Africa League last year

The National Basketball Association (NBA) says it removed Rwanda's army team from its African league because of US sanctions imposed on the country in March.

The NBA had previously said the Rwandan army-funded Armée Patriotique Rwandaise (APR) club would not participate in the 2026 Basketball Africa League (BAL).

However this is the first time the NBA has revealed the reasons behind the APR's removal.

The association was responding to complaints by two US senators, who sent a letter asking them to reconsider their partnership with the Rwandan team. The US placed sanctions on the Rwandan army, accusing it of fuelling the conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo in March.

The senators said the NBA risked "becoming complicit in sportswashing by accepting money from a Rwandan government that systematically abuses human rights".

Last week, the US also imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its support for the M23 rebel group which has seized control of large parts of eastern DR Congo. Rwanda denies backing the rebels despite overwhelming evidence.

Rwanda is an official BAL partner and pays the league to host its finals at the 10,000-seat BK Arena in the capital, Kigali.

The evidence that shows Rwanda is backing rebels in DR Congo

In the letter to the NBA dated 23 October, Democratic Senator Jeffrey Merkley and Republican counterpart Marsha Blackburn gave the association until 2 November to give a written response regarding its continued partnership with Rwanda.

"What is the NBA red line for accepting money from foreign governments that commit human rights abuses?" the senators asked.

Among other queries, they also questioned how the association could "reconcile its continued partnership with Rwanda with its purported commitment to justice".

In its response, NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum said the Rwandan team "had been withdrawn" from the BAL following the sanctions imposed earlier in the year, American sports website ESPN reports.

The NBA said the APR basketball club would remain barred while the US sanctions are in place.

The APR is one of Rwanda's top basketball teams and represented the country in the BAL in 2024 and 2025, when it came third. It was replaced by the RSSB Tigers this year.

The BAL is a pan-African basketball league established and co-organised by the NBA and the basketball's world governing body Fiba.

It is a professional league featuring 12 club teams from across the continent.

Rwanda has hosted all but one of the league's final and playoff matches since the inaugural match in 2021.

The NBA reportedly receives millions of dollars annually from the country for the marketing and partnership rights.

DR Congo has repeatedly condemned Rwanda's high-profile international sports deals, including with the NBA, European football clubs and Formula 1, asking them to end their campaigns.

It argues that these help Rwanda clean up its global image, while the conflict continues in eastern DR Congo.

DR Congo has been facing the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history

A British man who has tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo will be flown back to the UK.

It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths.

It is not clear when the flight will take place.

Earlier, a UK government spokesperson said there were "well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and that the risk to the public remains low.

Reuters news agency reported the infected man is a healthcare worker, citing an internal document BBC News has not seen.

Imported Ebola cases are extremely rare in the UK and have resulted in no deaths.

There have only been four confirmed cases of the virus in the UK - one, in 1976, resulting from a laboratory incident, and three involving health workers who were responding to an outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015.

A UK government spokesperson said: "The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated.

"Further information will be shared in due course as appropriate. The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low."

There have been more than 10,000 confirmed cases since the recent outbreak in DR Congo started in May, which has grown to become the second most deadly recorded spate of infections, behind the outbreak in West Africa.

It has since become the deadliest in the country's history, with a fatality rate of 48.6% reported at the end of last month.

Ebola can result in serious illness and death. Early symptoms include vomiting and diarrhoea but it can progress to organ failure and internal bleeding.

The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

The ongoing outbreak centred on DR Congo is fueled by the Bundibugyo variant of the virus.

There is no approved vaccine but the World Health Organisation said experts have recommended adding two new candidate drugs to an ongoing clinical trial.

The vaccines, one developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, and another by the firm Moderna, will join the trial once they are approved by Congolese health authorities.

It will be the first time jabs specifically designed to protect against the Bundibugyo virus are tested during an outbreak.

Since the outbreak, Ebola cases have also been confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.

MN202611_an9hii2dzc.t:
The devastating two-year civil war killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions

An Ethiopian-born American citizen has pleaded guilty to passing highly classified intelligence to Ethiopia, including information he hoped would help target and kill fighters from the Tigray region during the country's 2020-22 civil war.

Abraham Teklu Lemma, a former US contractor, admitted sharing dozens of classified documents and photographs with senior Ethiopian officials over more than two years, the US Department of Justice said.

"In doing so, he betrayed his oath, his colleagues, and his country, while jeopardizing our national security," said US Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

The 54-year-old faces up to 22 years in prison under a plea agreement.

Abraham had worked as a contractor at the State Department, Justice Department and National Reconnaissance Office, the agency responsible for US intelligence satellites.

Prosecutors said Abraham worked with senior figures in Ethiopia's political, military and intelligence establishments between 2021 and his arrest in August 2023.

He secretly removed classified material from secure government facilities, sometimes copying sensitive information into handwritten notes that he carried out of the buildings. He used his position as an IT administrator to extract electronic intelligence files.

"Much of the highly classified information Lemma shared with the Ethiopian government concerned an armed conflict in Ethiopia," prosecutors said.

The information included satellite imagery and details of military activities, which he passed to Ethiopian officials through encrypted messages.

The FBI said Ethiopian officials subsequently used intelligence supplied by Abraham in military operations.

Prosecutors said he hoped the information would help Ethiopia's military identify and kill paramilitary fighters.

"Lemma betrayed the United States to an extraordinary degree," said John Eisenberg, the US assistant attorney general for national security.

In one message to an Ethiopian official in December 2021, he wrote: "We have to finish these people once and for all, otherwise there will never be peace in Ethiopia," court papers showed.

Later that day, he shared further intelligence and urged the official: "Please send Dro[nes]."

The BBC has contacted the Ethiopian authorities for comment.

The revelations shed light on how sensitive American intelligence was passed to Ethiopian authorities during a devastating civil war that killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.

It was marked by widespread allegations of atrocities, including massacres, sexual violence and attacks on civilians.

A peace agreement signed in November 2022 ended the conflict, although fighting resumed in September after both sides accused each other of not respecting the terms of that deal.

How fresh fighting in Tigray could spark wider conflict in Ethiopia

Abraham was arrested in Maryland in August 2023 following an investigation into his handling of classified intelligence.

At the time, prosecutors alleged that he had removed security markings from intelligence reports and shared information with a foreign intelligence official.

In one exchange, the official asked him to continue providing assistance, to which Abraham replied: "Roger that!"

Pirro, the US attorney, said Abraham had abused his access to some of America's most sensitive intelligence.

She accused him of betraying his colleagues and country with prosecutors saying he "will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law".

Abraham pleaded guilty to conspiring to transmit national defence information to a foreign government.

His sentencing is scheduled for 14 April 2027.

MN202611_1avahir9v8.t:
Fans pay respects to Tenerife's De Miguel

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono says he is experiencing "the most difficult days of my life" after the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Tenerife player De Miguel, 30, died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

The world of football has paid tribute to De Miguel, a father-of-one who joined Tenerife in summer 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all games in European competition this week.

Owono's club issued a statement on the goalkeeper's behalf on Wednesday, explaining the 25-year-old "wishes to share a few words personally".

"These are the most difficult days of my life," Owono says in the statement.

"I struggle to find the words, and it is very hard for me to come to terms with what has happened.

"I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him.

"I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are all experiencing.

Earlier on Wednesday, FC Andorra team-mate Lautaro Spatz defended Owono and said he "would never intentionally hurt anyone" and had been "deeply affected" by De Miguel's death.

Writing on social media, centre-back Spatz said Owono was devastated.

Spatz paid tribute to De Miguel, then said of Owono: "Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

"In football, unfortunate incidents can happen but no-one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences."

Players from FC Andorra held a minute's silence before a voluntary training session on Wednesday. Owono was not at the session.

Football world mourns Tenerife striker De Miguel

Tenerife and Andorra were drawing 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time on Monday when the incident occurred.

Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel.

The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him, before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez to hospital.

Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned.

The goalkeeper, who had over 30,000 followers on Instagram on Tuesday morning, has since deactivated his account.

Police in Spain opened a routine investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel's death.

Under Spanish law, any death that is deemed non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.

Owono has made 47 international appearances for Equatorial Guinea.

The president of Equatorial Guinea's football federation, Venancio Tomas Micha, issued a statement on Tuesday offering "all our human and professional backing" to the player.

"As the involuntary protagonist of this tragic incident in the game, he is living through this situation with deep sorrow and distress," he added.

Jesus de Miguel joined Tenerife in 2025 on a three-year deal

On Tuesday, mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.

Tenerife said in a statement they will commence six official days of mourning, with all club activities suspended during this time.

The club's players, staff and officials will attend De Miguel's funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, Toledo.

Tenerife will also open their home ground on Saturday evening to allow supporters to "bid a fitting farewell".

"Jesus de Miguel's family would like to thank everyone for their messages of support and, from the bottom of their hearts, ask that their privacy be respected at this terrible time. May he rest in peace," added the club statement.

ST. JOHN’S, Antigua and Barbuda – President Paul Kagame has held talks with leaders from four Caribbean countries, exploring opportunities to expand Rwanda’s cooperation in trade, investment, tourism and other areas.

The meetings took place on the sidelines of the 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), hosted in Antigua and Barbuda from November 1 to 4.

Kagame met Jamaican Prime Minister Andrew Holness on November 2. Their discussions focused on strengthening cooperation in health, defence and tourism, as well as exploring opportunities in trade and investment.

Holness said the meeting offered an opportunity to identify new areas of cooperation and development between the two countries.

Kagame also met Antigua and Barbuda’s Prime Minister Gaston Browne, the Bahamas’ Prime Minister Philip Davis and St Vincent and the Grenadines’ Prime Minister Godwin Friday on November 3.

The engagements focused on bilateral relations and opportunities to expand economic and development cooperation. No specific agreements or investment commitments were announced.

The Caribbean meetings were part of a wider series of bilateral engagements that also included talks with Sri Lankan Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya and Eswatini’s Prime Minister Russell Mmiso Dlamini.

Kagame used the summit to call for greater investment in developing economies, challenging the perception that investing in the Global South carries greater risks than investing in developed markets.

Speaking during a high-level panel on November 2, alongside Holness and Samoa’s Deputy Prime Minister Mulipola Anarosa Ale Molioʻo, Kagame said investment was necessary to drive development, create jobs and equip young people with skills.

He argued that risks exist in all markets and can be managed through cooperation and the pooling of resources. The Commonwealth, he said, could help countries work together to unlock investment opportunities.

Kagame also stressed the importance of market integration, strong institutions and policies that connect the public and private sectors.

Holness, who joined the discussion, said governments needed to improve efficiency and their ability to deliver services and development projects.

Kagame also held talks with World Trade Organization Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala. They discussed Rwanda’s partnership with the WTO, regional trade and investment, market access for businesses and adding value to critical minerals.

The summit brought together leaders from the Commonwealth’s 56 member countries under the theme, “Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth.”

Discussions centred on trade, investment, climate resilience and sustainable development, including the economic challenges facing small island states.

Kagame attended the official opening ceremony on November 3 at the National Performing Arts Centre in St John’s, alongside King Charles III, Queen Camilla, Prime Minister Browne and other Commonwealth leaders.

He also participated in closed-door sessions of heads of government and attended a reception hosted by King Charles III following the Commonwealth Leaders and CEO Investment Summit.

Rwanda was represented at the ministerial level by Foreign Affairs Minister Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe.

Rwanda joined the Commonwealth in 2009 and hosted the organisation’s 26th summit in Kigali in June 2022. Kagame served as Chair-in-Office until 2024.

The 2026 summit is expected to conclude with a communiqué outlining the leaders’ shared priorities and commitments.

Rusororo Cemetery, which was originally expected to operate until 2029, is now projected to reach capacity sooner.

KIGALI – Rwandans may no longer be allowed to build concrete graves or use tiles to finish burial structures under new land-use regulations issued by the National Land Authority (NLA).

The rules prohibit concrete structures and tiled finishes in designated cemetery and crematoria zones, whether below or above ground. They also state that permanent structures are not allowed in these areas.

The restriction is contained in the second edition of the Land Use Master Plans’ Zoning Regulations , a document published in September 2026. It sets out what can be built, where development is allowed and which activities require special approval or are prohibited.

The cemetery provisions are among several changes affecting how Rwandans use their land, from building homes and commercial properties to establishing schools, hospitals, factories and agricultural facilities.

In Rwanda, burials generally take place in designated cemeteries rather than in family compounds or backyards, as is customary in some societies. Families typically pay for a plot or burial space, with fees varying from one location to another.

The cemeteries contain a wide range of grave designs. Some graves are elaborate structures resembling monuments, while others are modest: a raised patch of soil, sometimes marked with a simple cross to identify the burial place.

The differences in size and design often reflect the financial means of the bereaved family, with some able to afford elaborate structures while others opt for simpler graves.

The new rules do not, however, explain whether concrete graves already in existence must be removed or whether the restriction applies only to new construction.

Under the regulations, cemeteries and crematoria are classified as Public Facilities Zone PF6.

The permitted activities include cemeteries, crematoria, facilities such as pavilions and service rooms, and green spaces. However, the document adds that permanent structures are not allowed.

It specifically lists concrete structures and tiled finishes, both underground and above ground, among prohibited uses.

In practical terms, this could affect families who traditionally construct concrete tombs, build raised concrete structures over graves or use tiles to finish burial places.

The rules also prohibit industrial, commercial and residential activities within land designated for cemeteries and crematoria.

Some supporting facilities may be allowed after assessment. These include accommodation for cemetery caretakers, public facilities such as toilets and prayer halls at crematoria.

The regulations also address the location of cemeteries near wetlands. They require an environmental impact assessment where a cemetery is near a wetland and prescribe a buffer distance of 200 to 300 metres.

The document does not explain the environmental or public-health reasoning behind the specific prohibition on concrete graves. That is an issue the NLA may need to clarify, particularly because the rule touches on burial practices and family traditions.

The new document is not a separate national land-use master plan. It is an updated set of rules intended to guide the implementation of existing plans, including the Kigali City Master Plan and District Land Use Plans.

The country has a National Land Use and Development Master Plan covering the period 2020 to 2050. It sets out how land should be allocated for housing, agriculture, industry, infrastructure, environmental protection and other activities.

The zoning regulations translate that broad plan into practical requirements for individual plots.

For example, a person may own land but cannot automatically decide to build a factory, shopping centre or apartment block on it. The type of development allowed depends on the zone in which the plot is located.

The rules divide land uses into three categories: permitted, conditional and prohibited.

Permitted activities can proceed subject to applicable requirements. Conditional activities require assessment and approval by the City of Kigali or the relevant District One Stop Centre. Prohibited activities are not allowed in the designated zone.

The second edition updates and consolidates the earlier regulations. NLA officials have said the changes are intended to harmonise the implementation of Kigali’s master plan with district land-use plans, refine land-use categories and strengthen control over development.

The changes were announced during Rwanda Architecture Week in October.

One of the changes with a direct impact on residents concerns access to schools and health facilities.

Under the revised rules, education and research facilities (PF1) and health facilities (PF2) are permitted uses in all residential zones.

This means that schools, research institutions and health facilities can be accommodated in areas designated for housing, subject to the other applicable development requirements.

The change follows concerns that some residents have difficulty accessing essential services because nearby areas were not designated for schools and health centres.

Other public facilities have different requirements. Religious facilities, cultural and memorial sites, and sports and leisure facilities are conditional uses in residential areas. They must undergo assessment and receive approval before development.

The intention is to make essential services more accessible while ensuring that facilities are suitable for the neighbourhoods in which they are built.

The regulations also introduce specific conditions for high-end luxury villas and mansions in residential areas.

Such properties are now treated as conditional uses. This means that owners and developers cannot assume that they can construct them simply because they own a residential plot.

The proposed development must first be assessed and approved by the relevant planning authority.

The assessment is intended to establish whether the project is compatible with the surrounding area and meets applicable planning requirements.

This is particularly relevant for large properties that may include extensive gardens, swimming pools, guest houses, gyms and other facilities.

The regulations also provide requirements governing building heights, plot coverage, density, parking and the distance buildings must maintain from roads and neighbouring properties.

For example, the rules distinguish between low-density residential areas, rural residential zones and areas planned for higher-density housing.

A plot in a low-density residential area may have different building-height and development requirements from one in an area planned for apartments and other multi-family housing.

The regulations also encourage mixed-use development, where residential buildings, shops, services and other compatible activities are located closer to one another.

They place emphasis on pedestrian access, public transport and the provision of green spaces.

For someone planning to build a house, this means that checking the zoning classification of a plot is important before purchasing land or preparing construction plans.

A person who buys land expecting to build a particular type of property may discover that the proposed development is not permitted under the zoning requirements.

The revised regulations also affect industrial and agricultural activities.

In light industrial zones, factories with a pollution index above 20 per cent are not permitted. The distinction is intended to prevent activities that generate higher levels of pollution from operating in areas designated for lighter industrial use.

Agricultural land is also subject to controls intended to prevent its unnecessary conversion to other uses.

The regulations distinguish between agricultural and livestock zones and set conditions for activities that may be allowed alongside farming.

For example, facilities supporting agricultural activities, such as produce-drying facilities, stores, washing stations and agro-selling points, are subject to specific requirements.

This means that not every building or commercial activity can automatically be established on land designated for agriculture.

The new regulations make the zoning classification of a plot an important consideration for anyone planning to buy, develop or change the use of land.

Before investing in a property, buyers and developers need to establish what the land is designated for and whether their intended project is permitted, conditional or prohibited.

For conditional uses, approval must be obtained from the relevant planning authority. Meeting the conditions for one type of development does not automatically exempt a project from other requirements, including building standards, environmental assessments and parking provisions.

The regulations are intended to bring greater consistency to land-use planning across the country, but questions remain about how some provisions will be implemented.

In particular, the NLA needs to clarify how the prohibition on concrete grave structures will affect existing cemeteries, families planning new burials and projects that were already underway before the revised rules were published.

For many Rwandans, the cemetery provision may be the most immediately striking change. But the wider document has implications for anyone who owns land, intends to build a house, operates a business or plans to invest in property.

A Starlink satellite internet facility used by residents to communicate with the outside world, has been bombed

MINEMBWE – For nearly a month, residents of Minembwe in the mountains of South Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have been struggling to survive under a renewed military siege that has cut off essential supplies, restricted movement and left the sick and wounded with diminishing access to medical care.

Food shortages are worsening, medicines are running out, and traders face dangerous journeys through difficult terrain to bring basic commodities into the isolated highlands of South Kivu. Some families are reportedly struggling to obtain even the most ordinary household necessities.

The scale of the crisis is reflected in the soaring price of basic goods. A kilogram of salt, according to one resident quoted by local media, can cost as much as $30 (about Rwf 40,000) in some circumstances, according to people able to communicate with the outside world.

Ordinarily, salt is the cheapest essential item anywhere. It shouldn’t be more than US$3. Not in Minembwe.

The deteriorating situation was highlighted on November 3 by Bertrand Bisimwa, Vice-President of the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), during a meeting in Goma with James Swan, head of the United Nations peacekeeping mission in DRC, MONUSCO.

Bisimwa said the blockade had lasted nearly a month, leaving civilians without reliable access to food, humanitarian assistance and medicine.

He accused the government in Kinshasa of intensifying military operations in South Kivu and opening new fronts, in violation of commitments under the Doha peace process.

Forces enforcing the blockade included the Congolese army (FARDC), Burundian troops, Rwandan FDLR militia, foreign mercenaries and Wazalendo militia.

In this graphic video, a Wazalendo militia member is tomenting a group of Banyamulenge civilians. The speak in video makes several frightening statements against the victims. At one stage he points camera at a child, saying: “This one will also soon fight me”.

The humanitarian consequences are also described in detail in Whatsapp groups of Banyamulenge diaspora. Those in Minembwe report to their families that Minembwe’s hospital was struggling to treat the growing number of sick and wounded people because of limited resources.

Traders supplying the area are reportedly forced to use difficult routes through Uvira, Bijombo and Kamombo – all far away. Some carry goods over long distances on foot, exposing themselves to insecurity along the way.

The current crisis follows an earlier, prolonged blockade that began in October 2025.

In July 2026, Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC/M23 took control of Minembwe, ending that period of encirclement and allowing some residents to return.

But renewed military pressure has raised fears of another siege. By September, reports were already warning that government-aligned forces were preparing to re-establish restrictions around the highlands.

The latest escalation has also involved reported aerial attacks. Bisimwa said bombardments on November 2 and 3 caused deaths and injuries, while wounded residents could not reach medical supplies or treatment.

Some of the damage from latest government bombardments in Minembwe

On November 4, the FRN’s spokesperson, Lawrence Kanyuka, again accused government forces of using drones against Minembwe. He said two strikes had hit Minembwe Centre on the evening of November 3.

The diaspora association Mahoro Peace also reported attacks affecting Madegu, Ilundu and Gakenke, alleging that CH-4 drones were involved. The claims and reported casualty figures have not been independently verified.

Meanwhile, reports circulating on social media say a Starlink satellite internet facility used by residents to communicate with the outside world, has been bombed. It was established by members of the Banyamulenge diaspora.

The situation has revived concerns about the vulnerability of civilians caught between armed forces and competing military objectives. A resident quoted by Congolese media also criticised Twirwaneho fighters, accusing them of failing to ensure residents’ security or facilitate humanitarian assistance.

The resident called for the demilitarisation of the area, a neutral force to protect civilians, and safe passage for food, medicine and medical evacuations.

For Minembwe’s residents, the immediate issue is survival: access to food, healthcare and safe movement.

Without humanitarian corridors and an end to attacks on civilian areas, the renewed blockade risks deepening an already severe crisis.

A High-Level Forum of Women Leaders has convened at the Kiriri Presidential Palace in Bujumbura, the commercial capital of Burundi.

According to organisers, the 7th edition of the forum (November 4-5) has attracted high-profile personalities.

The First Lady of the Central African Republic, Brigitte Touadéra ( pictured above ) arrived in Bujumbura on November 3.

Burundi’s First Lady Angeline Ndayishimiye has been busy receiving her counterparts upon arrival at Melchior Ndadaye Airport.

Meanwhile several other women leaders are already in the country for the gathering.

Delegates at the forum seek to examine and address the challenges that limit the advancement and empowerment of women.

Deliberations are being guided by the theme; “Empowering young girls, a strategic lever for the development of human capital and strengthening resilience to climate change.”

The forum provides a platform for discussions on strategies to promote women’s empowerment, combat gender inequalities and gender-based violence, and enhance climate resilience.

Dr. Liliane Nkengurutse Executive Secretary of Burundi’s office of First Lady says the forum also aims to mobilize various actors around the obstacles to the fulfillment of women and girls, and to encourage concrete commitments in favor of their empowerment.

According to her the forum features the official launch of the “Building Resilience” campaign by the Organization of African First Ladies for Development (#OPDAD) and the International Trade Fair for Women’s Entrepreneurship of the Economic Community of Central African States (#CEEAC).

Burundi is gearing up for the forthcoming Presidential Elections scheduled for May 3rd 2027.

President Evariste Ndayishimiye has signed an order announcing the elections schedule.

According to Decree No. 100/167 of November 4, 2026, signed in Gitega, the first round of voting is scheduled for Monday, May 3, 2027.

In case of no winner with 50% of the vote, a second round is scheduled to take place on June 1st.

The text also specifies the voting procedures, the timetable for submitting candidacies, as well as provisions relating to the participation of the diaspora and Burundian military personnel on missions abroad.

Aspiring Presidential candidates are directed to submit their candidature to the Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI), from November 13 to 22.

The text specifies that no coalition of independents is permitted. An independent is considered to be any candidate who has not claimed affiliation with any political party for at least one year and who asserts independence from the usual political divisions, by presenting a personal societal project.

The election will be held by universal direct suffrage and secret ballot, in accordance with Article 56 of the Electoral Code.

The President of the Republic will be elected by a single-member two-round ballot.

To be elected in the first round, a candidate must obtain an absolute majority of the votes cast, i.e., 50% of the votes plus one.
