Taarifa Investigative Desk has reliably learned that President Felix Tshisekedi has ordered an immediate chopping of Bodyguards assigned to FARDC Generals.

The order comes at a time senior officers are increasingly defecting to the Front For Refoundation of Nation (FRN) a rebel movement led by former President Joseph Kabila.

“The FARDC General Staff is requesting that Generals with more than 14 bodyguards return the excess personnel along with their weapons and ammunition,” said a source familiar with the matter at the Army headquarters in the capital Kinshasa.

The source added, “Some [Generals] now retain two bodyguards, others three or four.”

Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) have recently suffered significant defections to the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) headed by Kabila a staunch critic of President Tshisekedi regime.

Brigadier General François Kamanzi ( pictured above ) defected to the FRN rebels movement on October 27. Later, Brigadier General Germain Katanga in Goma joined the rebels.

Additional reports cite senior figures like Colonel Dem Umba Ndolo Ghislain and Lieutenant Lemba Lula Arnold.

Meanwhile, about 700 soldiers including mid-level officers and lower ranking abandoned their deployment zones and joined the FRN-led rebellion.

Kabila compares Tshisekedi management of the state as though a clan leader, submerged in tribalism, corruption and mismanagement of state.

President Donald Trump has suffered a major political blow following the Democrats’ triumphant capture of majority seats in the Senate during midterm elections.

Democrats scooped 54% of the Senate seats trouncing Republicans that secured 44% of the seats in senate.

The blue wave sweeping the US in the midterm elections, with Democrats winning the Senate and heading for a big House majority, analysts consider it an end of Trumpism.

With both chambers under Democratic control, Trump faces the prospect of congressional negotiations and significant obstacles to advancing his remaining legislative priorities.

Economic concerns dominated the campaign, with Democrats capitalizing on dissatisfaction over grocery prices, health-care costs and Trump’s handling of the economy.

Republicans struggled to convince voters that the president’s policies were improving their financial circumstances.

The Senate results were especially consequential.

Democrats overcame a challenging electoral map, flipping at least four Republican-held seats in red states to erase the GOP’s 53-47 advantage and secure control of a chamber responsible for confirming presidential nominees and federal judges.

Democrats will gain subpoena power through congressional committees and greater leverage over federal spending, though Trump’s veto authority and Senate procedural rules will limit their ability to enact legislation without Republican support.

Democrats still need 60 Senate votes to have a complete lock on Capitol Hill because of the filibuster.

MN202611_yt3o8i05cg.t:
President Paul Kagame held bilateral discussions with five Commonwealth leaders on the third day of the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), in engagements that provide opportunities to strengthen diplomatic relations, explore economic cooperation and expand development partnerships.

The meetings brought Kagame together with Antigua and Barbuda’s Prime Minister Gaston Browne, Bahamas Prime Minister Philip Davis, Sri Lankan Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya, St. Vincent and the Grenadines Prime Minister Godwin Friday, and Eswatini Prime Minister Russell Mmiso Dlamini.

Although details of the individual discussions have not been publicly disclosed, such high-level engagements on the sidelines of CHOGM provide an opportunity for governments to identify shared priorities, discuss potential areas of investment and explore cooperation in sectors that directly affect economic growth and people’s livelihoods.

For Rwanda, engagement with these countries presents opportunities to strengthen South-South cooperation, particularly in trade, tourism, agriculture, education, technology, infrastructure development and private-sector investment.

The discussions also come at a time when the Commonwealth is placing greater emphasis on mobilising investment, improving access to development financing and building economic resilience, particularly for smaller and climate-vulnerable economies.

Ministers meeting ahead of the leaders’ summit called for stronger public-private partnerships, increased investment and more affordable financing to support sustainable development. Commonwealth

Opportunities across different economies

The engagement with Antigua and Barbuda and the Bahamas offers scope for Rwanda to explore cooperation with Caribbean economies, particularly in tourism, hospitality, climate resilience, renewable energy and the sustainable use of natural resources.

Both countries have economic interests linked to tourism and the ocean economy, areas in which experience-sharing could support Rwanda’s ambition to expand its tourism industry, attract international visitors and develop high-value investment opportunities.

Discussions with Sri Lanka could open opportunities for exchanges in agriculture, agro-processing, education, technology, manufacturing and tourism.

Sri Lanka’s experience in export-oriented industries and agricultural value chains could provide areas for knowledge-sharing, while Rwanda could explore opportunities to expand trade and business connections with South Asia.

With St. Vincent and the Grenadines, potential areas of cooperation include climate adaptation, agricultural development, renewable energy, disaster preparedness and tourism.

These are particularly relevant to countries seeking to strengthen their resilience against climate-related economic shocks.

Engagement with Eswatini, meanwhile, provides an opportunity to explore closer economic ties within the African context, including agricultural value addition, manufacturing, trade, skills development and investment cooperation.

These are potential areas of mutual interest rather than confirmed agreements arising from the meetings.

Executive session focuses on shared challenges

Beyond the bilateral engagements, Kagame participated in the first CHOGM 2026 Heads of Government Executive Session alongside host Prime Minister Gaston Browne and other Commonwealth leaders.

The closed-door meeting provides a platform for heads of government to deliberate on shared challenges, establish guiding principles for cooperation and consider collective responses to issues affecting member states.

The discussions are particularly significant as Commonwealth countries face interconnected challenges involving economic inequality, youth unemployment, food security, climate change, access to financing, technological transformation and sustainable development.

The Commonwealth’s 2026 agenda has also highlighted the need to move beyond recognising the vulnerabilities of smaller economies towards unlocking their potential through investment, innovation and stronger international partnerships. Commonwealth

For Rwanda, participation in these discussions and bilateral engagements offers an opportunity to strengthen its international economic relationships, expand diplomatic cooperation and identify partnerships that can translate into practical benefits for businesses, institutions and citizens.

While no specific agreements or investment commitments have been announced from the five meetings, their significance lies in creating high-level channels through which countries can advance shared development priorities, explore new economic opportunities and build relationships that may lead to future cooperation.

The Rotary Club is seeking to expand its community development initiatives through partnerships aimed at addressing local needs, empowering vulnerable groups and creating opportunities for young people, as Rwanda positions itself for a bigger role in international motorsport.

Charles Habba, representing the Rotary Club, said the organisation wants to use its network and partnerships to support practical community projects, particularly those targeting children, people with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.

He explained that the club’s work goes beyond bringing people together, focusing instead on identifying challenges within communities and mobilising resources to address them.

The club, which started with 14 founding members, is exploring initiatives that could use sports as a tool for inclusion, including activities supporting children living with disabilities and those battling cancer.

Habba also highlighted the importance of partnerships in delivering community projects, pointing to a possible collaboration involving access to piped water in Bugesera as an example of how Rotary can contribute to improving people’s living conditions.

He said the club is interested in working with other organisations, institutions and individuals willing to support initiatives that respond to community priorities.

Beyond traditional community service, the discussions also touched on Rwanda’s growing motorsport ambitions and the opportunities that could emerge from the country’s efforts to attract major international racing events.

Christian Gakwaya, President of the Rwanda Automobile Club, said motorsport should not be viewed exclusively as a competition for professional drivers or wealthy enthusiasts, but as an industry capable of creating opportunities across several professional fields.

He pointed out that motorsport requires engineers, mechanics, technicians, vehicle specialists, event managers and other professionals, creating room for young people to build careers beyond driving.

Gakwaya emphasised the importance of establishing academic and technical pathways that can prepare young Rwandans to participate in the sector, including through specialised training and partnerships with educational institutions.

He also highlighted the potential for local vehicle manufacturing and automotive innovation, arguing that Rwanda’s motorsport ambitions should contribute to developing domestic technical capacity rather than relying entirely on imported expertise.

However, he noted that achieving these ambitions requires investment in infrastructure, skills development and a supportive environment for the automotive industry.

The broader vision is to ensure that major sporting ambitions translate into lasting economic and social benefits, including employment, technical knowledge, entrepreneurship and opportunities for young people.

For Rotary, the community dimension remains central: ensuring that development initiatives reach people who need support and that partnerships produce tangible improvements in people’s lives.

The convergence of community service, sports and economic development presents an opportunity for organisations to work together in building a more inclusive future for Rwanda.

Ku wa 2 Ugushyingo 2026, Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika zatangaje ko Perezida Donald Trump yamenyesheje Kongere ya Amerika n’u Rwanda icyemezo cy’uko igihugu gishobora gukurwa muri gahunda y’ubucuruzi izwi nka African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), guhera ku wa 1 Mutarama 2027.

Ni icyemezo gishobora kugira ingaruka ku bicuruzwa by’u Rwanda byoherezwa ku isoko rya Amerika, ariko kugira ngo dusobanukirwe n’icyo bivuze, ni ngombwa kubanza kumenya AGOA icyo ari cyo, icyo yari imariye ibihugu bya Afurika n’icyo u Rwanda rushobora gutakaza.

Icy’ingenzi ni uko iyi gahunda itarebana n’ubucuruzi gusa, ahubwo inafitanye isano n’impaka zimaze imyaka myinshi hagati y’ibihugu bikomeye n’ibihugu bya Afurika ku bijyanye n’uburyo byakubaka ubukungu bwabyo.

AGOA ni impine y’amagambo African Growth and Opportunity Act, mu Kinyarwanda twavuga ko ari gahunda yashyizweho na Amerika igamije guteza imbere ubukungu n’amahirwe y’ubucuruzi ku bihugu bya Afurika yo munsi y’Ubutayu bwa Sahara.

Yashyizweho na Kongere ya Amerika mu mwaka wa 2000, igamije gufasha ibihugu bya Afurika kubona amahirwe yo kugurisha ibicuruzwa byabyo ku isoko rya Amerika, byungukira ku kuba ibicuruzwa byujuje ibisabwa byinjirayo bidatanze imisoro ya gasutamo.

Mu buryo bworoshye, iyo igihugu cyemerewe muri iyi gahunda, ibicuruzwa byacyo bishobora kwinjira muri Amerika bitishyuriwe imisoro imwe n’imwe isanzwe yishyurwa n’ibicuruzwa biva mu bindi bihugu.

Ibi biha abacuruzi n’abashoramari bo muri Afurika amahirwe yo guhangana ku isoko rya Amerika, kuko ibicuruzwa byabo bishobora kugurishwa ku giciro kisumbuyeho.

AGOA itanga amahirwe ku bicuruzwa birenga 1,800, birimo imyenda, ibikomoka ku buhinzi, ibikomoka ku nganda, amabuye y’agaciro n’ibindi.

Ariko kugira ngo igihugu gikomeze kuyungukiramo, kigomba kuzuza ibisabwa birimo guteza imbere ubukungu bushingiye ku isoko, kubahiriza amategeko, guteza imbere ubwisanzure mu bya politiki, kurengera uburenganzira bw’abakozi, kurwanya ruswa no gukuraho inzitizi ku bucuruzi n’ishoramari biva muri Amerika.

Bivuze ko AGOA atari ubufasha butagira ibisabwa, ahubwo ari gahunda y’ubucuruzi ihuza amahirwe yo kubona isoko rya Amerika n’ibisabwa n’ubuyobozi bw’icyo gihugu.

Mu myaka yashize, u Rwanda rwakoresheje amahirwe ya AGOA mu kohereza ibicuruzwa bitandukanye muri Amerika, birimo ikawa, icyayi, ibikomoka ku buhinzi, ibikoresho bikozwe mu bukorikori n’ibindi bicuruzwa.

Gukurwaho muri iyi gahunda bishobora gutuma ibicuruzwa by’u Rwanda byari byemererwaga kwinjira muri Amerika nta misoro ya gasutamo bisabwa kwishyura iyo misoro isanzwe ibireba.

Ibi bishobora kugira ingaruka ku biciro, inyungu z’abohereza ibicuruzwa hanze, ubushobozi bwo guhangana ku isoko ndetse n’ishoramari mu bigo byari byarubatse ubucuruzi bishingiye kuri ayo mahirwe.

Abakora ubucuruzi bw’ikawa n’icyayi bashobora kuba mu bahura n’ingaruka, cyane cyane abari barateguye kongera umusaruro n’ubucuruzi bwabo ku isoko rya Amerika.

Iyo ibicuruzwa bisabwa kwishyura imisoro itari isanzweho, bishobora gutuma abaguzi bo muri Amerika bahitamo ibindi bicuruzwa biva mu bihugu biri muri AGOA cyane ko byo igiciro kitakwiyongera.

Nk’umuryango ukorera mu rwego rwa Kiliziya Gatolika, twemera ko buri muntu afite agaciro n’icyubahiro akwiriye.

Yakomeje avuga ko Komisiyo ayoboye iteganya gukorana n’imiryango itandukanye kugira ngo ifashe abahoze mu mitwe yitwaje intwaro kongera kwisanga muri sosiyete nyarwanda, kwiyubaka no kugira uruhare mu kubaka u Rwanda rufite abaturage bishimye.
